answer: Verdict: FY26's faster cash-NPAT growth (+7% vs +4% in FY25) was higher quality. The earnings engine rotated from margin-led to volume-led, jaws turned positive, and the result absorbed a rising impairment charge instead of relying on a falling one. FY25 NII growth (+5%) came from margin: NIM +9bp on average interest-earning assets of only +1%, and CBA flagged 7bp of that as composition (lower liquids/pooled facilities, NII-neutral); the underlying +2bp was Capital/Replicating +9bp minus funding costs -7bp from deposit competition. FY25 NPAT also had a -9% impairment tailwind. FY26 reversed the pattern: NII +7% was driven by AIEA +$92bn (+8%; lending +7%, business loans +10%) with NIM -3bp to 2.05%, and impairment became a +9% headwind; pre-provision profit growth doubled from +3% to +6%. CBA's FY26 margin bridge reconciles the -3bp as: liquids -3bp (NII-neutral); asset pricing -5bp (home -4, business/institutional -1, competition); funding costs flat; portfolio mix +2bp; Capital, Replicating and Other +5bp (replicating +4, capital hedges +1); Treasury & Markets -2bp - so underlying NIM was stable and the reported compression is composition, not franchise erosion. The results presentation groups the bars differently (Liquids & repos -4bp, T&M -1bp; liquids +$15bn, repos +$11bn) but sums to the same -3bp; I prefer the profit announcement's fuller split. Competitive pressure migrated from the liability side (FY25 funding costs -7bp) to the asset side (FY26 asset pricing -5bp), offset each year by rate-hedge earnings - a cyclical, not franchise, offset. Supporting the higher-quality read: growth at/above system in all five core domestic product categories; underlying cost-to-income fell 30bp to 44.9%; ROE rose 50bp to 14.0%; and the 8bp loan-loss rate remains below FY23 (12bp) and FY24 (9bp), with realised losses low, non-performing exposures down 4bp to 0.69% of TCE, and the increase driven by collective provisions for geopolitical/macro uncertainty and portfolio growth. Against it: provision coverage fell from 1.60% to 1.53% of credit RWA, 2H26 impairment annualised at 9bp with consumer arrears rising, the margin retains a +5bp hedge tailwind, and other operating income included a CommInsure milestone payment and a Gemini IPO fair-value gain.

key_facts.fact: FY26 cash NPAT from continuing operations rose 7% to $10,982m, versus +4% to $10,252m in FY25; pre-provision profit rose 6% in FY26 versus 3% in FY25.

Net profit after tax from continuing operations 10,133 7 10,252 9,836 4
Cash net profit after tax increased 7% to $11bn, pre-provision profit increased 6% to $16.5bn and return on equity rose to 14.0%.

key_facts.fact: FY26 NII growth of 7% was volume-led: average interest-earning assets rose $92bn (8%) while NIM fell 3bp to 2.05%.

citations.quote: Net interest income was $25,586 million, an increase of $1,563 million or 7% on the prior year. The result was driven by a $92 billion or 8% increase in average interest earning assets to $1,246 billion, partly offset by a 3 basis point decrease in net interest margin to 2.05%.

key_facts.fact: FY25 NII growth of 5% was margin-led: NIM rose 9bp to 2.08% while average interest-earning assets rose only 1%.

citations.quote: The result was driven by a 9 basis point increase in net interest margin to 2.08% and a $9 billion or 1% increase in average interest earning assets to $1,154 billion.

key_facts.fact: 7bp of FY25's 9bp NIM rise was NII-neutral composition; the underlying rise was only 2bp.

citations.quote: Excluding a 7 basis point increase in margin from a reduction in lower yielding liquid assets and institutional pooled facilities, which have a broadly neutral impact on net interest income, net interest margin increased 2 basis points.

key_facts.fact: FY25's underlying margin gain was hedge-driven: Capital, Replicating and Other +9bp against funding costs -7bp from deposit competition.

citations.quote: Capital, Replicating and Other: Increased margin by 9 basis points driven by the net impact of the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 5 basis points) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 4 basis points).
Funding costs: Decreased margin by 7 basis points driven by increased deposit price competition.

key_facts.fact: CBA's FY26 margin bridge shows the 3bp reported compression was compositional (liquids), with underlying NIM stable: asset pricing -5bp offset by portfolio mix +2bp and Capital, Replicating and Other +5bp; Treasury & Markets -2bp.

citations.quote: Excluding growth in liquid assets, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, net interest margin was stable.

Asset pricing: Decreased margin by 5 basis points driven by home lending pricing (down 4 basis points) and business and institutional lending pricing (down 1 basis point), primarily reflecting the impact of competition.

Capital, Replicating and Other: Increased margin by 5 basis points driven by higher earnings on the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 4 basis points) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 1 basis point).

key_facts.fact: The FY26 results presentation shows the same -3bp bridge (208 to 205bpts) grouped as Liquids & repos -4bp and Treasury & Markets -1bp, driven by +$15bn average liquids and +$11bn average institutional repos.

citations.quote: Lower margin largely due to growth in liquids and repos - competition offset by hedge earnings
+$15bn increase in average liquid assets and +$11bn increase in average institutional repos in FY26 vs FY25.

key_facts.fact: Loan impairment expense swung from a -9% tailwind in FY25 ($726m, 7bp loan-loss rate) to a +9% headwind in FY26 ($788m, 8bp).

Loan impairment expense as a percentage of average gross loans and acceptances (GLAA) increased 1 basis point to 8 basis points.

key_facts.fact: FY26 jaws were positive: underlying cost-to-income fell 30bp to 44.9%, and CBA grew at or above system in all five core domestic product categories.

citations.quote: Underlying operating expenses to underlying operating income ratio decreased 30 basis points from 45.2% to 44.9%.
In FY26, CBA grew at or above system in each of our five core domestic product categories: home lending, business lending, consumer finance, household deposits and business deposits.

key_facts.fact: FY26 other operating income (+4% to $4,638m) included one-off items: a CommInsure sale milestone payment and a Gemini IPO fair-value gain.

citations.quote: mainly driven by higher insurance income, including a milestone payment recognised in relation to the sale of Commonwealth Insurance Limited (CommInsure General Insurance)
a fair value gain on our investment in Gemini following its Initial Public Offering

key_facts.fact: The 2H26 exit run-rate deteriorated on credit: loan impairment expense annualised at 9bp of GLAA, with home and personal loan arrears at 0.73% and 1.72%.

citations.quote: Loan impairment expense annualised as a percentage of average GLAA increased 3 basis points to 9 basis points.
Home loan and personal loan arrears increased to 0.73% and 1.72% respectively reflecting cost-of-living pressures

key_facts.fact: FY25 NPAT growth leaned on a lower impairment charge; CBA's own framing of the two years differs on this point.

limitations: CBA does not quantify the dollar split of FY26 NII growth between volume and margin; the 8% AIEA / -3bp NIM decomposition is directional only.
The dollar size of the FY26 one-off items in other operating income (CommInsure milestone payment, Gemini IPO fair-value gain) is not disclosed.

The split of the $62m FY26 loan impairment expense increase between collective (forward-looking) provisions and individually assessed charges is described qualitatively, not quantified at Group level.
FY25 comparatives in the FY26 documents were restated to conform with current-period presentation; all comparisons here use the cash continuing-operations basis.

The profit announcement and the results presentation allocate the reverse-repo margin drag to different bridge bars (Treasury & Markets vs Liquids & repos); both sum to -3bp, and the analysis prefers the profit announcement split.
FY25's loan-loss-rate comparison to FY26 uses CBA's printed rates (7bpts vs 8bpts); underlying decimals are not disclosed, so the true gap could be smaller or larger than 1bp.
